items.title: Dick Spottswood interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 13, 2023
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Yeah. Well look at Irving Mills and Duke Ellington. ... [INTERVIEWEE] At least there the personalities of the historical figures are well enough known that you can pretty well guess as to what’s going on.

ctx.x: went in that direction. I mean those are distinctions we create because music composition has become a business instead of an art. And when there’s a business there’s money being made, and when there’s money being made you’ve got to decide how to divide it up and that’s really what those things are good for. So yes, I think composer credits are very important. I discovered fairly early on that if I looked at those on records that I didn’t know often times it would tell me — on jazz records especially — it would…
Yeah. Well look at Irving Mills and Duke Ellington. People got their fingers into the money pie throughout the music history.

At least there the personalities of the historical figures are well enough known that you can pretty well guess as to what’s going on. And certainly there has always been a bunch of collaboration between colleagues. Somebody’ll say well he’d fix that up if he’d done thus and so in measure 32, you know that kind of thing happened. Does that entitle you to a composer credit? In some cases it does, but it’s kind of up to the decisions that people make at the time. When Johnny Hodges introduced “Rent Party Blues” or…
